lower_bound.quote: Since $|E|<|V|$, the multigraph $G$ contains no cycle and no loop: a cycle or a loop through $v$ vertices already uses at least $v$ edges, so a graph containing one would have at least as many edges as vertices, forcing $|E|\ge|V|$ — impossible.
lower_bound.witness: COUNTEREXAMPLE to the quoted claim (and NON-SEQUITUR in its justification: a cycle/loop on $v$ vertices forces $|E|\ge v$, not $|E|\ge|V|$, since the other $|V|-v$ vertices may carry no edges). Take $n=2$, $u=1/7$, geometric pieces $q_0=1/7$, $q_1=2/7$, $q_2=4/7$. Xiang Yu uses $K=2$ cuts, both inside the piece of length $4/7$, splitting it into $0.2,\;0.2,\;4/7-0.4=0.1714\ldots$. Then $M=5$ parts sorted: $a_1=2/7=0.2857$ (piece 1), $a_2=0.2$ (piece 2), $a_3=0.2$ (piece 2), $a_4=0.1714$ (piece 2), $a_5=1/7$ (piece 0). Pairs: $P_1=\{a_1,a_2\}$ gives edge $\{1,2\}$; $P_2=\{a_3,a_4\}$ has both parts in piece 2, i.e. a LOOP at vertex 2. Here $|E|=2<3=|V|$, so the quoted implication fails; every admissible tie-breaking gives the same loop. Since the loop sits at vertex $n=2$, the component $T$ containing vertex $n$ is not a loop-free tree, so it admits no proper $\pm1$ colouring with 'the two signs are opposite' on each pair, and the chain $u\le|\Xi|\le\sum\varepsilon_i+[M\text{ odd}]a_M$ is not established.
lower_bound.load_bearing: The whole lower bound rests on $T$ being a loop-free tree: the 2-colouring, the cancellation $|s(\pi(a_{2i-1}))a_{2i-1}+s(\pi(a_{2i}))a_{2i}|=\varepsilon_i$, and hence $|\Xi|\le D(A)$ all require it. Without it Lemma 4 (hence $D\ge u$ for every Xiang Yu reply) is unproved.

parsed.notes: Reduction (Lemma 2) and upper bound (Lemma 5: subset-sum gap plus overlay/cross-pairing with mark count m-1=n) check out. Lower bound's graph step is false: |E|<|V| does not exclude loops/cycles; an explicit n=2 refinement produces a loop at the top vertex.
